units: <cite ref="Chagigah 2a:5">Ib. 2ᵃ</cite> <he>ס׳ באחת מעיניו</he> blind in one eye.
<cite ref="Taanit 21a:8">Taan. 21ᵃ</cite> <he>ס׳ משתי עיניו</he> blind in both eyes.
<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 36:2">Ex. R. s. 36</cite> <he>פקח וס׳ שהיו וכ׳</he> a seeing and a blind man that were walking &c.

<cite ref="Bava Batra 12b">B. Bath. 12ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Niddah 20b:28">Nidd. 20ᵇ</cite> <he>כס׳ בארובה</he>, v. <cite ref="A03015"><he>אֲרוּבָּה</he></cite>; a. fr.—Pl. <he>סוּמִים</he>, <he>סוּמִין</he>.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 53:14">Gen. R. s. 53</cite> <he>בשעה … הרבה ס׳ נתפתחו</he> when Sarah was remembered, many childless women were remembered with her, … many blind persons had their eyes opened.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 53:8">Ib.</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Genesis 21:19">Gen. XXI, 19</cite>) <he>הכל בחזקת ס׳ עד וכ׳</he> all men are to be considered as blind, until the Lord opens their eyes.
Snh. 34ᵇ שלא בס׳ cannot be performed by blind persons; a. fr.—Fem. סוּמָא, סוּמָה.
<cite ref="Ketubot 17a:1">Keth. 17ᵃ</cite> <he>הרי … או ס׳</he> suppose the bride is lame or blind.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sotah 2:5:10">Y. Sot. II, end, 18ᵇ</cite> <he>הוא סומא היא ס׳</he> whether he (the husband) be blind, or she, (the law is the same).
<cite ref="Chullin 139b:14">Ḥull. 139ᵇ</cite>; a. fr.—[Ch. <cite ref="O00336"><he>סוֹמָא</he></cite>, v. <cite ref="O01080"><he>סַמְיָא</he></cite>.]
